"Today in France a billionaire pays less taxes proportionally than a nurse or a firefighter," explains Yakoub. She challenges the foundations of France's fiscal system, arguing that the growing concentration of wealth and preferential tax treatment of the ultra-rich are undermining the constitutional principle of equality before taxation. news.summary: A aprovação do fim da escala 6x1 , com a redução da jornada de trabalho de 44 para 40 horas semanais, repercutiu na imprensa internacional, que destacou que a votação foi uma vitória do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva às vésperas do 2º turno das eleições no Brasil. O jornal espanhol El País escreveu no título que “dezenas de milhões de trabalhadores conquistam um segundo dia livre no Brasil, uma vitória política para Lula”. Na Argentina, o jornal Clarín classificou a aprovação como “jogada política de Lula: Brasil aprova redução da jornada de trabalho, a menos de duas semanas do segundo turno das eleições”. Notícias relacionadas: Fim da escala 6x1 traz esperança de mais tempo para família e saúde. CUT elogia fim da “massacrante” 6x1; CNI quer revisar PEC aprovada . Senado aprova fim da escala 6x1 e redução da jornada de trabalho. O também argentino La Nacion disse que a votação é “a grande aposta de Lula antes do segundo turno”, acrescentando que “o filho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro mudou de posição e anunciou seu voto favorável 48 horas antes da sessão". O jornal inglês Financial Times , especializado em economia e finanças, destacou que os legisladores brasileiros “votaram para abolir uma semana de trabalho de seis dias na maior economia da América Latina”. O jornal diz que a votação foi uma “vitória para Lula” próxima ao segundo turno eleitoral, acrescentando ainda as críticas dos grupos empresariais que reclamam de aumento de custos. “Terminar a semana de trabalho de seis dias alinhará o Brasil com muitas nações de renda mais alta, onde as horas de trabalho diminuíram à medida que a produtividade e a eficiência melhoraram”, escreveu o Financial Times . O também britânico The Guardian aponta vitória de Lula com a aprovação e calcula que a mudança pode afetar até 30 milhões de pessoas no Brasil. “A proposta começou como um movimento do TikTok chamado Vida Além do Trabalho, fundado por um assistente de farmácia que entrou na política após seu sucesso e mais tarde foi abraçado por Lula”, escreveu o The Guardian . Mudança de posição A imprensa estrangeira ainda lembrou que o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que disputa o 2º turno contra Lula, era contrário à proposta de emenda à constituição (PEC) que acaba com a 6x1, mas acabou mudando de posição poucos dias antes da votação. “Mesmo depois de mudar sua posição, Bolsonaro disse na terça-feira que ‘apoia algo ainda melhor’, referindo-se a uma proposta alternativa que há muito tempo defendia em que o pagamento seria baseado nas horas realmente trabalhadas”, acrescentou o The Guardian. A agência de notícias dos Estados Unidos (EUA) Associated Press ( AP ) apontou que o único voto contrário foi “do ex-vice-presidente Hamilton Mourão, que atuou durante o governo do presidente Jair Bolsonaro”. A AP explicou que os aliados do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) “deixaram de bloquear a medida popular para que ele não fosse prejudicado em sua disputa acirrada contra Lula”. Manifestantes participam de ato pelo fim da escala 6x1 e caminham pela Avenida Brasil, na Zona Norte do Rio de Janeiro. Foto: Tomaz Silva/Agência Brasil Aprovação no Senado O plenário do Senado concluiu a aprovação da PEC do fim da 6x1 na noite de quarta (14), com 75 votos a favor e apenas um contrário. A oposição, que era contrária à aprovação da matéria, mudou de lado após o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), pautar o tema no plenário. Em entrevista à TV Jovem Pan, o líder do PL na Câmara, deputado Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ), afirmou que, se eleito, Flávio Bolsonaro deve aprovar a PEC 12/2026 , que prevê um contrato “por hora trabalhada”. Entenda a PEC O texto da PEC que acaba com a 6x1 prevê descanso remunerado obrigatório de dois dias por semana, em jornada máxima de 5x2, sem redução salarial, e também reduz a atual jornada de trabalho de 44 para 40 horas semanais, com uma regra de transição total de 14 meses. >> Saiba mais detalhes sobre como vai funcionar o fim da 6x1 Pelo texto, 60 dias após a promulgação da emenda constitucional, as empresas deverão adotar a escala 5x2 e reduzir a jornada máxima para até 42 horas semanais de trabalho. Depois de mais 12 meses, a jornada será reduzida para 40 horas semanais.

news.summary: French Football Federation's ethics body calls for neutrality amid student protests.

news.title: 2026 Midterms: Georgia's Ossof-Collins showdown lies at the heart of the battle for US Senate
news.summary: In Georgia, Democrat Jon Ossoff’s seat is one of the key contests in the US mid-term elections on 3 November. In this state, which was won by Donald Trump in 2024, the incumbent senator is facing Republican Mike Collins. Our reporter Leela Jacinto visited Manuel’s Tavern, a historic bar in Atlanta that has been frequented for decades by Democratic politicians. There, patrons watched the debate between the two candidates.

news.title: Delegates walk out as Israeli president addresses summit
news.summary: Officials from more than 10 countries walked out during an address by Israeli President Isaac Herzog at a summit in Baku

news.title: France charges teen shooter citing revenge for bullying in school
news.summary: A 14-year-old charged with attempted murder in France after wounding a principal and a teacher in a school shooting this week said he acted out of revenge for bullying, prosecutors have said. The incident, at a middle school for 11- to 15-years-olds, is not thought to have any link with ongoing high school protests nationwide to demand better learning conditions.

news.title: Do hospital, papa volta a celebrar missa após cirurgia no pulmão
news.summary: Segundo o Vaticano, Leão 14 passou a noite bem, tomou café da manhã e retomou atividades; exames indicam boa recuperação

news.title: US consumer inflation hotter than expected as midterms loom
news.summary: US consumer inflation was hotter than anticipated in September, government data showed Wednesday, as Washington's continued war with Tehran pushed energy costs higher, deepening strains on American households ahead of next month's midterm elections. The uptick underscores voter worries over high costs of living, and comes as President Donald Trump is campaigning in US states to shore up support for his Republican Party as it tries to retain control of Congress.

news.title: Israel ex-security chief sues Netanyahu over October 7 claims
news.summary: The former head of Israel's Shin Bet domestic security agency on Wednesday sued Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for defamation weeks before elections in a row over responsibility for Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack. Netanyahu, who polls show in a tight race to stay in power in the October 27 election, has been hammered by the opposition for failing to prevent the attack, the deadliest day in Israeli history. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports.

news.title: Police and protesters face off in Albania on third day of anti-govt demonstrations
news.summary: Demonstrators and riot police clashed in Albania's capital on Thursday in a third straight day of violence triggered by student protests calling for better university conditions and Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation. Originally sparked by a luxury tourism project linked to US President Donald Trump's family in the country's south, the demonstrations have occasionally flared into violence amid ongoing calls for Rama's resignation. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Philip Turle tells us more.

news.title: Former US generals push to stop 'barbaric' firing squad execution livestream
news.summary: A group of 72 retired US generals, admirals, and other high-ranking military officers have urged authorities to cancel plans to livestream the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hassan – bringing legal arguments and the dangerous consequences such a broadcast would have. A government execution has never been broadcast or livestreamed, according to death penalty experts, and the US military ​has not executed anyone by firing squad since 1945.

news.title: Was Neanderthal life violent? This wound suggests lethal fighting was more common
news.summary: A 75,000-year-old Neanderthal spear wound may be evidence violence shaped human life far earlier than thought.

news.title: Ukraine struggles with Starlink and US satellite data as missiles hit Kyiv
news.summary: Ukraine on Wednesday accused the United States of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv's military response through changes to the Starlink system it uses on the battlefield. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called on US tech billionaire Elon Musk to restore Starlink, which Kyiv says has been slowed down.

news.title: Fort Hood shooter’s firing squad execution will not be livestreamed, Trump says
news.summary: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he was cancelling plans to livestream the firing squad execution of a convicted military base shooter – a project that had sparked outrage in the United States. Nidal Hasan is scheduled to be executed on December 3 at Fort Hood in Texas, where he killed 13 people in 2009.

news.title: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
news.summary: A search and rescue operation is under way in the Black Sea after the latest attack in the area.

news.title: Trump anuncia que no habrá retransmisión en directo de la ejecución del atacante de Fort Hood
news.summary: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha anunciado este jueves que la ejecución de Nidal Malik Hasan, el psiquiatra militar condenado a muerte por matar a tiros a 13 militares en la base de Fort Hood en 2009, no será finalmente retransmitida por respeto a la "gente de buena voluntad" que no quiere verle morir.

news.summary: One year after the former prime minister's death, Kenyans are reflecting on his contribution to democracy and national reconciliation. Odinga's "handshakes" with his political rivals remain the subject of much debate.

news.title: Pink October in France: A toxic debate?
news.summary: Pink October – the French version of Breast Cancer Awareness Month – is at the centre of a political storm here in France, after one MP said she refused to wear a pink ribbon, calling the month "utterly cynical". We dive into her reasoning, discuss the history of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and learn how to look out for "pinkwashing".

news.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
news.summary: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

news.title: Trump says Fort Hood shooter execution won't be livestreamed after bipartisan backlash
news.summary: The announcement earlier this month from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that Hasan's execution would be public prompted significant blowback from both Republicans and Democrats, with many pointing out that the images could be used to fuel radicalization.

news.title: Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
news.summary: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

news.title: Haiti: Capoeira classes aim to promote peace
news.summary: An association in Haiti is organising capoeira classes – an Afro-Brazilian martial art – in an attempt to reduce community violence and promote social reintegration. The Observers team spoke to its founder, Rodney Jean Marc, who said their doors are open to everyone, “even children in armed gangs”. The initiative takes place as the country's security situation has worsened in recent years.

news.summary: To discuss the ongoing conflict between the Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed coalition, we speak to Jules Grange Gastinel, a researcher at France's CNRS research body specialising in the Houthi movement. He tells us why the conflict has escalated and what the Houthis want.

news.summary: Em Salvador, pequeno empresário fechou as portas de mercadinho ao calcular que dois funcionários a mais na escala inviabilizariam o negócio.

news.title: NATO to address drone attacks in the Black Sea after seven missing off Romania
news.summary: NATO will put drone strikes in the Black Sea on its agenda at a meeting next week, officials said Thursday, following two new attacks and the disappearance of seven people. Incidents involving civilian vessels in the Black Sea have been on the rise off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania in a suspected spillover from Russia’s war in Ukraine.
